sections.overview: The Glaucous Gull is an Arctic-breeding gull that also nests on islands in tundra lakes. It shares genus Larus with the Common Gull and Lesser Black-backed Gull profiled here.
sections.identification: Adults are large, bulky and very pale, with pale-grey wings, pink legs and a yellow bill; the wingtips lack black. Compared with the darker Lesser Black-backed Gull, its pale wings and pink legs are distinctive.
sections.habitat: It nests on Arctic cliffs and coasts, and sometimes on remote islands in inland tundra lakes. Outside the breeding season it uses marine waters, freshwater lakes, fields and landfills.
sections.diet: This opportunistic omnivore takes marine invertebrates and fish, but also carrion, refuse, insects, berries and other birds or their eggs.
sections.behavior: Pairs may nest alone or in colonies, while nonbreeding birds gather in flocks to feed and rest. The species also follows fishing vessels and scavenges at processing plants and dumps.
sections.reproduction: Both parents build a shallow nest and incubate a clutch of one to three eggs. Young leave the nest soon after hatching but remain nearby until they can fly.
sections.ecology: By hunting seabirds and their eggs as well as scavenging, it acts as both predator and consumer of carrion in Arctic food webs.
sections.conservation: The 2018 global IUCN assessment classified it as Least Concern and reported a stable population trend.
